chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the fasting person who applies kohl.
He said: There is no harm in it; it is not food nor drink.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani's chain, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that applying kohl does not break the fast because it is not consumed as food or drink, a ruling that distinguishes it from substances ingested orally. This establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) for the fast, affirming that external applications do not nullify the state of fasting unless they reach the stomach. This view is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between *akl* (eating) and *shurb* (drinking) versus other forms of nourishment or medicine.
